investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both sets of nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~134–146 seconds across all three checks, no VM was ever assigned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Likely] The 4 non-peerpods nodes have a node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec that restricts scheduling exclusively to peerpods-capable nodes, so capacity exhaustion on those 2 nodes is a hard ceiling with no fallback.
[Possible] A node that previously held kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was cordoned, drained, or removed from the cluster, reducing the total schedulable VM slots below the demand level.
[Possible] A quota or resource limit at the namespace or cluster level is preventing additional kata.peerpods.io/vm allocations even if raw node capacity exists.

[Lower likelihood] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec is misconfigured or was recently changed to target a label that no longer matches any node, artificially shrinking the eligible node pool to only the 2 peerpods nodes.

investigation.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigation.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness successfully routed the aura-gpt-5-5 test request to the backend API endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test, but the backend was unable to reach the underlying model provider at the time of the eval run. The API returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This caused the harness to surface a 502 to the eval runner, setting ok=false, provider=null, and resolvedModel=null for aura-gpt-5-5, which in turn caused allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, violating the model-matrix expected-output contract assertions at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=10346, well within the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, ruling out a latency-driven timeout as the cause.
possibleCauses: Primary — transient provider-side unavailability for the OpenAI/GPT-5 provider at the time of the eval run (2026-07-24T22:50:21Z). The 424 error message explicitly states 'AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider' and 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits', indicating a backend-to-provider connectivity or quota issue rather than a credential or eval infrastructure problem.

investigation.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame and no image URL artifact. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream billing rejection.
investigation.rootCause: The OpenAI account used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1981–1986) called /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2, the OpenAI API immediately rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached and type billing_limit_user_error. The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames before receiving the error, then emitted a generation_error frame carrying the billing message, and never emitted generation_completed or an image URL. This is an external account/billing configuration failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or application logic. No user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability probe environment.

All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot publication pipeline rather than the public website itself.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot on disk is 600 minutes old (double the allowed maximum), indicating the workflow either did not trigger, was skipped, or failed to publish an updated file. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publication pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing website outage is present — all three sibling page checks passed.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 600' — the single violated assertion that caused the eval to fail.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=600, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was generated by GitHub Actions but is 10 hours old.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — the contract the snapshot violated.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, which is looser than the contract's max of 300 — a potential configuration inconsistency worth noting.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses — the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from statusSnapshotEvidence(payload) — the age value comes directly from the live remote JSON, not from eval infrastructure.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions scheduled workflow that publishes status.json did not run or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published file in place and causing snapshotAgeMinutes to accumulate to 600.
GitHub Actions workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deploy or file commit step) failed silently, so the remote JSON was not updated even though the workflow appeared to complete.
GitHub Actions workflow was manually cancelled, paused, or had its schedule disabled, preventing automatic re-publication.

Configuration mismatch: the feature registry at infra/evals/status/features.json line 383 sets staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, while the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 enforces max=300 — if the workflow runs on a cadence aligned to 360 minutes, it would still violate the stricter contract assertion.
CDN or GitHub Pages caching served a stale version of status.json to the eval runner despite a successful workflow publish, causing the eval to observe an older generatedAt timestamp.

investigations.title: Image Generation Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame and no image URL artifact. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream billing rejection.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the eval probe at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1981–1986) called /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2, the OpenAI API immediately rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached and type billing_limit_user_error. The stream emitted generation_start and generation_progress frames before receiving the error, then emitted a generation_error frame carrying the billing message, and never emitted generation_completed or an image URL. This is an external account/billing configuration failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or application logic. No user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval infrastructure failure scoped to the observability probe environment.
proof: failed-check.message: OpenAI error code billing_hard_limit_reached with type billing_limit_user_error is the first error in the check message, directly preceding the assertion failures.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes array contains [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent, confirming the stream never reached completion.
failed-check.evidence: The generation_error frame data carries code GENERATION_FAILED and the full OpenAI billing error JSON, proving the error originated from the OpenAI API response.
failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent is false, consistent with the stream being terminated by a billing error before any image artifact was produced.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=728 — the check completed in under one second, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation failure.

expected-output.contract: The contract requires frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent to equal true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 339–344); neither assertion was satisfied.
possibleCauses: Primary: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner environment has reached its hard spending limit, causing all image generation requests to be rejected immediately with billing_hard_limit_reached.
Secondary: The API key configured for the eval runner is associated with a different OpenAI account or project than intended, and that account has a lower or exhausted billing limit.
Tertiary: A billing limit was recently lowered or a quota reset did not occur, causing a previously passing eval to begin failing at this point in the billing cycle.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If re-running the eval after the billing limit is resolved still produces a generation_error frame with a non-billing error code, the root cause would be a different upstream failure rather than the billing limit.

If the OpenAI account dashboard shows the hard limit has not been reached and there is remaining quota, the billing_hard_limit_reached error would need to be explained by a misconfigured API key pointing to a different account.

If sibling checks that also call OpenAI APIs (e.g., public-chat-stream) are simultaneously failing with the same billing error, that would strengthen the billing account hypothesis; if they are passing, it could indicate the image generation API key is separate and specifically exhausted.
If the eval passes immediately after the billing cycle resets without any manual intervention, that confirms the cause is a billing cycle exhaustion rather than a permanent account misconfiguration.

Consider a dedicated billing-health check eval that periodically verifies the OpenAI account usage is below a configurable threshold (e.g., 80% of hard limit) and warns before the limit is reached, preventing surprise eval failures.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returns 502/424 provider_account_unavailable
investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. The other model, aura-claude-sonnet-4-6, passed cleanly. This is a localized eval failure scoped to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route; no sibling checks failed and no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness successfully routed the aura-gpt-5-5 test request to the backend API endpoint POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test, but the backend was unable to reach the underlying model provider at the time of the eval run. The API returned HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This caused the harness to surface a 502 to the eval runner, setting ok=false, provider=null, and resolvedModel=null for aura-gpt-5-5, which in turn caused allPassed=false and failedModelCount=1, violating the model-matrix expected-output contract assertions at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334.
proof: failed-check.evidence: results[1] for aura-gpt-5-5 shows ok=false, provider=null, resolvedModel=null, and error containing 'POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test failed with 502' and inner code 'provider_account_unavailable'.
failed-check.evidence: allPassed=false, failedModelCount=1, failedModels=['aura-gpt-5-5'] — directly matching the two violated contract assertions.
failed-check.message: '1/2 models returned the expected response; Expected evidence assertion failed: allPassed expected true but got false; failedModelCount expected 0 but got 1'.

failed-check.evidence: results[0] for aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 shows ok=true, provider='anthropic', resolvedModel='aura-claude-sonnet-4-6', messageSample='hello from aura' — confirming the eval infrastructure itself and the Anthropic provider path are healthy.

expected-output.contract: assertions require allPassed equals true and failedModelCount equals 0 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 333–334); both are violated by the observed evidence.
source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1936: runner iterates over args.models and calls the runtime/test endpoint per model, confirming aura-gpt-5-5 was exercised as a discrete model slot.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=10346, well within the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, ruling out a latency-driven timeout as the cause.
possibleCauses: Primary — transient provider-side unavailability for the OpenAI/GPT-5 provider at the time of the eval run (2026-07-24T22:50:21Z). The 424 error message explicitly states 'AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider' and 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits', indicating a backend-to-provider connectivity or quota issue rather than a credential or eval infrastructure problem.

Secondary — the aura-gpt-5-5 model identifier may be misconfigured, deprecated, or not yet fully provisioned in the backend model registry, causing the provider resolution to fail (provider=null, resolvedModel=null in the result). A transient error would typically still resolve the model; null values suggest the provider lookup itself failed before or during the LLM call.
Tertiary — a backend-side rate limit, quota exhaustion, or account suspension specific to the GPT-5 provider account used by AURA's harness, surfaced as a 424 at the time of this eval run.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both sets of nodes. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~134–146 seconds across all three checks, no VM was ever assigned, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState). This is an eval-detected infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 134s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the call that triggers pod scheduling; failure here prevents any downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the pod never started.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are both marked required=true; degradedAfterFailures=1 means a single failure triggers a degraded signal for the remote-agents feature.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource is fully consumed on both eligible nodes — all in-flight or already-running remote agent pods have claimed the available VM slots, leaving zero capacity for new scheduling requests.

investigations.title: published-observability-snapshot eval fail: snapshotAgeMinutes 600 exceeds max 300 — GitHub Actions workflow has not published a fresh snapshot in ≥10 hours
investigations.summary: The eval for check published-observability-snapshot failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json reported snapshotAgeMinutes=600, which violates the expected-output contract assertion requiring snapshotAgeMinutes <= 300 (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482). All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure to the snapshot publication pipeline rather than the public website itself.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json has not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot on disk is 600 minutes old (double the allowed maximum), indicating the workflow either did not trigger, was skipped, or failed to publish an updated file. This is an eval-detected staleness condition scoped to the snapshot publication pipeline; no evidence of a user-facing website outage is present — all three sibling page checks passed.
proof: failed-check.message: 'snapshotAgeMinutes expected <= 300 but got 600' — the single violated assertion that caused the eval to fail.

failed-check.evidence: snapshotAgeMinutes=600, maxAgeMinutes=300, source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true, generatedAtPresent=true — the snapshot exists and was generated by GitHub Actions but is 10 hours old.
expected-output.contract: assertion { path: 'snapshotAgeMinutes', max: 300 } defined at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 — the contract the snapshot violated.

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:383: registry config shows staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, which is looser than the contract's max of 300 — a potential configuration inconsistency worth noting.

sibling.public-observability-page, sibling.public-models-page, sibling.public-marketing-pages: all three sibling checks passed with HTTP 200 responses — the public website is reachable and the failure is isolated to snapshot freshness.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:2168-2173: the runner fetches the snapshot via publicJsonUrl(args.publishedSnapshotUrl) and derives snapshotAgeMinutes from statusSnapshotEvidence(payload) — the age value comes directly from the live remote JSON, not from eval infrastructure.
possibleCauses: Most likely — GitHub Actions scheduled workflow that publishes status.json did not run or did not complete successfully within the last 300 minutes, leaving the previously published file in place and causing snapshotAgeMinutes to accumulate to 600.
GitHub Actions workflow ran but the publish step (e.g., a GitHub Pages deploy or file commit step) failed silently, so the remote JSON was not updated even though the workflow appeared to complete.
GitHub Actions workflow was manually cancelled, paused, or had its schedule disabled, preventing automatic re-publication.

Configuration mismatch: the feature registry at infra/evals/status/features.json line 383 sets staleAfterMinutes=360 for this check, while the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 482 enforces max=300 — if the workflow runs on a cadence aligned to 360 minutes, it would still violate the stricter contract assertion.
CDN or GitHub Pages caching served a stale version of status.json to the eval runner despite a successful workflow publish, causing the eval to observe an older generatedAt timestamp.
